questions.stem: According to the passage, what year was the Supreme Court decision Plyler v. Doe, which granted children of families in the U.S. illegally the right to attend public school?
questions.evidence: children of families living in the United States illegally have had the right to attend public school based on a 1982 Supreme Court decision
questions.explanation_ko: 1982년 대법원 판결에 따라 불법 체류 가정의 자녀도 공립학교에 다닐 권리를 가져왔다고 나와 있습니다.

questions.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is NOT listed as something the Saugus policy requires new immigrant families to provide?
questions.evidence: The policy requires new students to share immigration records. Families must sign a residency statement and provide housing and identity documents.
questions.explanation_ko: 이민 기록, 서명한 거주 진술서, 주거·신분 증명 서류는 언급되지만 은행 계좌 명세서는 언급되지 않았습니다.

questions.stem: What can be inferred from the fact that a Nicaraguan woman needed six months to register her 8-year-old child?
options: The Saugus policy has made registering children easier for all families.
The Saugus policy's document requirements can act as a real barrier that delays or blocks even eligible children from enrolling.
All Nicaraguan families in Saugus have been denied enrollment permanently.
The policy applies only to high school students, not younger children.
questions.evidence: it took six months to register her 8-year-old child because of the document requirements
questions.explanation_ko: 서류 요건 때문에 등록에 6개월이 걸렸다는 사례에서, 이 정책이 자격이 있는 아동에게도 실질적인 장벽으로 작용할 수 있음을 추론할 수 있습니다.

questions.stem: Why does the author mention that the Supreme Court's conservative majority has already overturned previous decisions on abortion rights and race-based college admissions?
options: To give context for why supporters of the 1982 Plyler v. Doe decision fear it could also be overturned
To argue that abortion and college admissions are unrelated issues
To criticize the Supreme Court's decisions on those topics directly
To explain the history of Oklahoma's education department
questions.evidence: The Supreme Court’s conservative majority has already overturned previous decisions on abortion rights and the use of race for admissions in higher education.
questions.explanation_ko: 이 배경 설명은 1982년 Plyler v. Doe 판결 지지자들이 그 판결도 뒤집힐 수 있다고 우려하는 이유를 보여 주기 위한 것입니다.

questions.stem: In the passage, what does "unconstitutional" mean in "it is unconstitutional to deny children an education"?
options: against the principles of the country's constitution
questions.evidence: it is unconstitutional to deny children an education based on their immigration status
questions.explanation_ko: unconstitutional은 국가 헌법 원칙에 어긋난다는 뜻입니다.

blanks.sentence_ko: 그들은 또한 Plyler v. Doe로 알려진 판결에 이의를 제기할 가능성을 제기한다.
그는 그 정책이 기존 거주 규정을 강화하는 것일 뿐 이민자를 배제하려는 의도는 아니라고 8월 회의에서 말했다.
여러 학교 시스템은 학생의 이민 신분을 확인하지 않겠다며 반발했다.
학교는 그 학군에 있는 모든 아이들을 환영하고 교육해야 합니다, 라고 Sellstrom은 말했다.

key_points: Since 1982, the Supreme Court's Plyler v. Doe decision has guaranteed children of families living in the U.S. illegally the right to attend public school, but some conservative politicians now question that right.
Supporters fear the decision could be challenged nationally, especially given the Supreme Court's recent reversals on abortion rights and race-based college admissions.

In Saugus, Massachusetts, a new school admissions policy requiring immigration and residency documents has, according to civil rights lawyers, created barriers that delay or block even legally eligible children from enrolling.

Some conservative groups and state officials, including in Oklahoma, have pushed to track or restrict education for children of immigrants, though similar attempts have failed so far in Tennessee and Texas.
main_idea: A 1982 Supreme Court decision guarantees public education for children regardless of immigration status, but conservative politicians and some local policies are increasingly challenging that right, creating new barriers for immigrant families.
restate_sentence: The justices said it is unconstitutional to deny children an education based on their immigration status.
